sources.entry: ZNC - Advanced IRC bouncer. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 C++/deb

summary.one_liner: ZNC is an advanced IRC bouncer written in C++ that stays connected to IRC servers on your behalf and replays missed messages to your clients.
summary.what_it_does: ZNC runs as a persistent server that holds IRC connections open while you are offline, then replays buffered channel messages when you reconnect. Clients connect to ZNC with a username:password server password, and users can run multiple networks. Configuration is created interactively with `znc --makeconf` and can be changed at runtime through IRC commands such as `/msg *status`, with SIGUSR1 forcing a config rewrite. Functionality is extended through modules, which can be written in C++, Python (via the ModPython global module) or Perl (via ModPerl). Optional features include SSL/TLS, Cyrus SASL authentication, ICU character encodings, and Boost.Locale UI translation. The README covers build requirements, CMake-based installation, file locations, and where to get help on the #znc channel on Libera.Chat.
use_cases: keep an IRC connection online while offline
replay missed IRC messages on reconnect
run a shared IRC bouncer for multiple clients
host IRC access for several users
write custom IRC bot or bouncer modules in Python or Perl
notable: Buffer replay of recent channel messages on client reconnect, with an option to keep buffers after replay
Modules can be written in C++, Python, or Perl
Configurable via IRC commands and a config file, with optional webadmin and controlpanel modules mentioned
configure.sh wrapper accepts old ./configure parameters for migration to CMake
caveats: Building from source requires several toolchain and optional library dependencies (GCC 8 or clang 5, CMake 3.13, and more for optional modules)
The README advises against editing the config file while ZNC is running
Some features depend on optional libraries such as OpenSSL, Python, Perl, or ICU
